set.body:
`meta_contrasts()` (R/metafuns.R:184) does:

    weighting <- match.arg(weighting)

and then never uses it. The pooling calls are `meta_fixef(tab)` and
`meta_Fcontrasts(tab)`, both without `weighting`, so `meta_fixef()` falls back
to its own default (`"inv_var"`).

A caller passing `meta_contrasts(cres, weighting = "equal")` therefore gets
inverse-variance pooling with no warning and no error. `meta_betas()` does use
its `weighting` argument (`do_fixef(se, beta, weighting)`, R/metafuns.R:~370),
so the two are inconsistent.

Pre-existing; predates the #220 work, which only made the argument reachable
from a single definition. Surfaced by review of PR #221.

`meta_Fcontrasts()` takes no `weighting` at all (it pools p-values via
Stouffer), so the fix is either to forward `weighting` to `meta_fixef()` and
document that it does not apply to F-contrasts, or to drop the argument from
`meta_contrasts()` if per-call weighting was never intended.

Either way it should not silently accept a value it discards.
set.title: meta_contrasts(weighting=) is accepted then silently ignored
